items.streamTitle: Higher subgroup AI accuracy sometimes reflected differing case mix
items.streamSummary: In two opioid-risk models, an apparently stronger AUC in Black patients narrowed after covariate matching. Subgroup accuracy gaps can reflect data distributions, not just algorithm quality.
items.attribution: Ladhania et al. — npj Health Systems

items.streamTitle: Driving scenes needing explanation drew somewhat longer descriptions
items.streamSummary: Analysis of 1,103 automated-driving annotations found explanation length moderately tracked perceived need (r=0.374), but prediction was weak. Driver comprehension and safety were not tested.
items.attribution: Kim et al. — Scientific Reports

items.streamTitle: A simple interaction model predicted constrained-space choices
items.streamSummary: An online restroom-choice study used statistical-physics models to estimate site preferences and predict occupancy across layouts. Model fit does not establish individual motives or real-world generalization.
items.attribution: Franckart et al. — Scientific Reports

items.streamTitle: EU Arctic strategy prioritizes monitoring and critical infrastructure
items.streamSummary: The European Commission's October 20 Arctic strategy adds maritime security, monitoring and infrastructure resilience priorities. Announced initiatives have not yet demonstrated operational results.
items.attribution: European Commission — official Arctic strategy announcement

items.streamTitle: AI language-learning satisfaction tracked perceived service support
items.streamSummary: Survey modeling of 978 AI language-learning users linked perceived service quality and support to satisfaction and reported performance. No causal improvement in tested language ability was established.
items.attribution: Lee, Li and Bi — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications

items.streamTitle: Brain-based cognition models predicted modest, variable shares of performance
items.streamSummary: A review found brain-based models often explained about 10–40% of cognitive variation, with lower estimates in cross-dataset tests. Imaging predictions are not direct measures of thought or causal mechanisms.
items.attribution: Christensen et al. — Communications Psychology (review)

items.streamTitle: Hong Kong cohort identified 35 predictors of later resilience
items.streamSummary: A longitudinal study of 26,210 people linked 35 earlier health, social and personal factors to later self-reported resilience. The design does not show that changing those factors causes resilience.
items.attribution: Ning et al. — Nature Mental Health

items.streamTitle: UNIDIR released new national security-and-defence AI strategy guidance
items.streamSummary: UNIDIR's 81-page October 19 guidelines distinguish strategy-development procedures from technical, legal and political requirements. The document offers governance guidance rather than evidence of policy effectiveness.
items.attribution: Afina, Mannsperger and Madziwa — UNIDIR guidelines

items.streamTitle: No tested input-noise method improved accuracy or reached 95% coverage
items.streamSummary: A groundwater forecasting experiment found accuracy–coverage trade-offs under simulated input noise. None improved baseline accuracy or achieved nominal interval coverage.
items.attribution: Shiri et al. — Scientific Reports

items.streamTitle: Mineral-law study distinguishes safeguards from demonstrated policy outcomes
items.streamSummary: A legal analysis finds tools linking mineral allocation, environmental obligations and strategic supply, but documents potential gaps between formal compliance and real outcomes.
items.attribution: Li et al. — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications

items.streamTitle: Park cooling and visitors' comfort reports followed different nonlinear patterns
items.streamSummary: A Shenzhen analysis linked satellite data to 11,109 public reviews. Physical and perceived cooling were not simply proportional; reported design thresholds are exploratory.
items.attribution: Zhao and Wang — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications

items.streamTitle: Changing mazes slowed navigation, not clearly rule learning
items.streamSummary: A virtual-maze study of 132 people showed reduced gains in route and time efficiency under changing layouts. The optimal-rule learning difference was inconclusive.
items.attribution: Tolchennikova et al. — Scientific Reports

items.streamTitle: Fast evacuation model trained on 100,000 simulated earthquake scenarios
items.streamSummary: Using 48 bridges in a real city network, researchers built a faster approximation of simulated evacuation time. Real-world evacuation outcomes were not validated.
items.attribution: Kim et al. — Scientific Reports

items.streamTitle: Stroke lesions weaken a brain signal linked to goal feedback
items.streamSummary: EEG in 68 stroke patients linked caudal anterior cingulate damage with weaker reward-positivity signals. Neural localization does not establish broad motivational outcomes.
items.attribution: Oerlemans et al. — Nature Communications

items.streamTitle: NATO emphasizes implementing lessons rather than simply collecting them
items.streamSummary: The October 14 official conference account stressed converting operational observations into institutional action. It did not report demonstrated performance gains.
items.attribution: NATO Allied Command Transformation — official report

items.streamTitle: AI agents learned hidden game rules but still exhausted common resources
items.streamSummary: OpenSocialJax found eight language models could learn environmental rules yet failed to sustain cooperation in shared-resource tasks. The results are simulations of agents, not human evidence.
items.attribution: Guo et al. — arXiv preprint (OpenSocialJax)

items.streamTitle: Hurricane spending losses tracked damage and outages more than storm category
items.streamSummary: Daily transaction analysis across 21 hurricanes and 7,987 ZIP codes found roughly two days of sales losses and recovery within about ten days for surviving firms. Infrastructure disruption predicted impact better than storm category.
items.attribution: Agarwal et al. — Nature Communications

items.streamTitle: Pessimism predicted engagement with only one of six conspiracy narratives
items.streamSummary: Among 2,506 Twitter users, pessimism related to engagement with one system-blame conspiracy narrative, not five others. Optimism and task-measured judgment bias showed no comparable links; causality was not tested.
items.attribution: Piksa et al. — Scientific Reports

items.streamTitle: Natural sounds showed more consistent well-being benefits than human sounds
items.streamSummary: A review of 194 studies and meta-analysis of 66 found fairly consistent positive associations for natural sounds; human sounds depended more on context. Behavioral and social outcomes were studied less often.
items.attribution: Guo et al. — npj Urban Sustainability (systematic review and meta-analysis)

items.streamTitle: Brief diaries gave AI a moderate signal of depression, not a diagnosis
items.streamSummary: In 108 participants, LLM depression scores from short diary transcripts moderately tracked surveys and clinical interviews. The study tested measurement validity, not diagnostic accuracy or patient outcomes.
items.attribution: Ringwald et al. — npj Digital Medicine

items.streamTitle: Oncology AI summaries reduced reported workload but remained incomplete
items.streamSummary: In a small oncology workflow study, clinicians reported lower workload and about three minutes saved per case, but only 63.6% of AI summaries were complete. Benefits remain exploratory.
items.attribution: van Koevorden et al. — npj Digital Medicine

items.streamTitle: Disaster-linked demand spikes may overwhelm remote mental-health support
items.streamSummary: Analysis of 138,471 Mexico City mental-health service interactions found sharp short-term demand changes near public-health and disaster events, including one 2,651% daily spike. The study is observational.
items.attribution: Garibay Rubio et al. — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications

items.streamTitle: Conflict-misinformation ensemble reported high scores on four benchmarks
items.streamSummary: An ensemble using text, imagery and affective features reported 94.66%–98.23% accuracy across four misinformation datasets. Results were benchmark-based and do not establish live conflict performance.
items.attribution: Muhammad et al. — Scientific Reports

items.streamTitle: Researchers proposed testing whether agreeable AI weakens tolerance for criticism
items.streamSummary: A new Perspective argues that overly agreeable AI may undermine learners' tolerance for corrective feedback. It defines ways to test the claim but reports no new empirical evidence of harm.
items.attribution: Chen et al. — npj Digital Medicine (Perspective)
